column3: The Hebrew first names silence as a noun; BSB uses three verbal commands.
The Hebrew has head in the singular; BSB has heads.
The Hebrew names Your hidden ones; BSB says those You cherish.
The Hebrew explicitly names a heart and cutting a covenant; BSB says one mind and forming an alliance.
The Hebrew pictures them as an arm for Lot’s sons; BSB says lending strength.
The Hebrew calls Kishon a torrent; BSB says River.
The Hebrew says they became dung rather than like dung as BSB does.
The Hebrew names a rolling wheel; BSB says tumbleweed.
The Hebrew says fill their faces with shame; BSB says cover.
The Hebrew separately names shame and perishing; BSB combines them as perish in disgrace.
